auditor_falsifiability.why_this_matters: A static audit that reports zero is worthless unless it can be shown to report non-zero when non-zero is present. This auditor initially reported a FALSE ZERO three times, and each defect was found and fixed rather than accepted.
defects_found_and_fixed_in_the_auditor: It scanned only for pyreadstat.<reader>(...) and so missed the reader entirely, because the broker calls it through a local variable. Every module would have looked falsely clean.
It then missed the self.pyreadstat.<reader> attribute form, still reporting zero.
It then missed the ternary that actually binds the alias (an ast.IfExp, not an ast.Attribute), still reporting zero. Only after all three fixes did it correctly report 1 reader call.

positive_control.conclusion: The same auditor reports 2 raw-path reader calls on a file that has them, so the count of 0 inside the C4 closure is a real negative rather than a broken query.

residual.statement: The C4 decoder route is clean: zero raw path strings reach pyreadstat, and exactly one governed physical open exists. Raw-path reader calls persist ONLY outside the C4 closure, in the WVS7 projection materializer.
residual.not_claimed: This audit does not assert that the WVS7 materializer is safe, in-closure, or correctly governed. It asserts only that it is outside the closure this audit covers.
